text: Você vem com a gente hoje à noite?
glossEn: Are you coming with us tonight?
notes: Marker: você, the everyday T-level address in Brazilian Portuguese, plus colloquial a gente (we).

text: O que você vai fazer no fim de semana?
glossEn: What are you going to do on the weekend?
notes: Marker: você as everyday informal address.
Marker: você plus the colloquial sentence-initial clitic in Me liga; casual spoken Brazilian Portuguese.
Marker: você; minimal pair with O senhor já almoçou?.

text: Cadê você? Já cheguei no bar.
glossEn: Where are you? I'm already at the bar.
notes: Marker: você with the colloquial question word cadê and colloquial chegar no.

text: O senhor pode me ajudar, por favor?
glossEn: Could you help me, please, sir?
notes: Marker: deferential address o senhor in place of você; maps to polite.

text: A senhora deseja mais alguma coisa?
glossEn: Would you like anything else, madam?
notes: Marker: deferential address a senhora; pair with the male o senhor version.

text: Bom dia, doutor Silva. Como o senhor está?
glossEn: Good morning, Dr. Silva. How are you?
notes: Marker: title address doutor Silva plus deferential o senhor.

glossEn: Have you had lunch yet, sir?
notes: Marker: deferential o senhor; minimal pair with Você já almoçou?.

text: Muito obrigado! Você me salvou hoje.
glossEn: Thank you so much! You saved me today.
notes: Trap: obrigado is a fossilized thanks formula and sets no register; você fixes the sentence as casual.

text: O senhor pode avisar o João: “me liga amanhã”?
glossEn: Could you let João know, sir: 'call me tomorrow'?
notes: Trap: the quoted me liga is casual spoken register, but the frame addresses the hearer as o senhor; the frame's register governs.

text: O trem para São Paulo sai às oito horas.
glossEn: The train to São Paulo leaves at eight.
notes: Third-person statement with no addressee; no register marked.

text: Chove muito em Manaus em janeiro.
glossEn: It rains a lot in Manaus in January.
